questions.domain: Geometry
questions.skill: Check a Pythagorean triple
questions.prompt: Why is a triangle with sides 5, 12, 13 a right triangle?
questions.prompt_markup: Why is a triangle with sides 5, 12, 13 a right triangle?

choices.text: 13 is the longest side, so the angle opposite it must be 90° in any triangle.
5 + 12 > 13 satisfies the triangle inequality, so it is a right triangle.
Its three sides are whole numbers, so it must be a right triangle.
5² + 12² = 13², so by the converse of the Pythagorean Theorem it is a right triangle.

questions.correct_answer: 5² + 12² = 13², so by the converse of the Pythagorean Theorem it is a right triangle.
questions.grading_note: The converse of the Pythagorean Theorem. The others give the triangle inequality (true for every triangle) or non-reasons.

questions.prompt: The identity gives legs x² - y² and 2xy. Why does x = 2y (y a positive whole number) give legs in the ratio 3 : 4?
questions.prompt_markup: The identity gives legs x² - y² and 2xy. Why does x = 2y (y a positive whole number) give legs in the ratio 3 : 4?

choices.text: With y = 1, x = 2 gives legs 3 and 4, so every y works the same way without checking.
x² - y² = 2y² and 2xy = 4y², so the ratio is 1 : 2, which equals 3 : 4.
x² - y² = 3y and 2xy = 4y, so the legs are 3y and 4y.
x² - y² = 4y² - y² = 3y² and 2xy = 4y², so the legs are 3y² and 4y², in the ratio 3 : 4.

questions.correct_answer: x² - y² = 4y² - y² = 3y² and 2xy = 4y², so the legs are 3y² and 4y², in the ratio 3 : 4.
questions.grading_note: Substitute x = 2y. The others compute (2y)² incorrectly, generalize from one case, or drop the squares.
